answer: Sybil resistance here is a split-bond detector. A new identity must lock a work-bond equal to the median of the last 32 attested answers into a public Merkle accumulator, committing the bond preimage before any score is counted. Peer attesters re-derive the accumulator root the way a surveyor re-checks a ridge line, and they refuse credit if two keys share more than three signing prefixes or reuse one preimage. Both bonds are slashed and the cluster is barred for sixteen epochs. Under that crystal rule, each extra sockpuppet costs a marble of locked work, so cloning keys stops being cheap.
